name: Custom BIMAX

lead: Custom BIMAX refers to bimaxillary jaw surgery, where upper and lower jaws are repositioned, using a design made specifically for the patient, such as individually planned cutting guides or plates. In forum discussions it is listed among custom facial procedures that people combine to change facial proportions.

Surgeons plan jaw surgery with scans, photographs and software that can predict the post-operative face shape. Published detail on custom guides specifically is limited in the general references used here, so the practice is described mainly through surgical planning in general.

paras: Patients typically work with a surgical team that uses radiographs, photographs and planning software, then undergo operations on the upper and lower jaw. Recovery involves a period on liquid diet and several weeks before return to work, with bone healing continuing for months.
Reported complications of jaw surgery include bleeding, swelling, infection and nerve injury causing numbness, usually temporary but rarely permanent. Recovery restrictions last around eight weeks.

chain: Upper and lower jaws repositioned with custom guides or plates
angle.text: Surgeons move the upper and lower jaw into a planned position, and custom guides or plates are intended to match that plan to the individual patient. People pursue it for facial proportions as well as bite.

lead: Custom BIMAX is a term used in looksmaxxing forums for bimaxillary jaw surgery performed with patient-specific (custom) planning hardware, in contrast to standard off-the-shelf plates. It aims to reposition the upper and lower jaw to change facial balance, projection and bite.[1]

Orthognathic surgery planning involves a multidisciplinary team, radiographs and photographs, and software that can predict post-surgical face shape, which also helps explain the plan to patients. The Wikipedia overview of orthognathic surgery lists custom and 'super' bimax options among osteotomy variants and notes the rise of 3D facial design systems as people increasingly fund surgery themselves.[2]
In a looksmax.org thread, one member describes planning a series of custom procedures, including custom bimax, custom wraparound, cheeks, brow and rhinoplasty, as part of an aim to model.[1]
infobox: Initial healing 2-6 weeks; bone remodelling further 2-4 months

paras: Jaw osteotomies can address the upper jaw, lower jaw or both, with both being most common. Jaw surgeries have been performed since the 1940s, and Hugo Obwegeser popularised the bilateral sagittal split osteotomy.[2]
Teams use radiographs, photographs and software that predicts the post-surgical face.[2]

Initial healing takes 2-6 weeks, with bone remodelling taking a further 2-4 months and recovery rules followed for about eight weeks. Complications can include bleeding, swelling, infection (reported up to 7%) and nerve damage causing numbness.[2]
No studies found specific to the custom bimax label. Orthognathic surgery in general is an established field with a substantial literature.

timeline.event: Jaw osteotomies begin to be performed.[2]
Raffaini introduces jaw surgery under local anaesthesia with IV sedation.[2]
